title: Pre-build AC decision is code, not prose (built, pending operator decision)
context: Eleven changes shipped without a written promise because the building agent chose the exemption by label.
decision: Code decides what code can decide: whether anything observable changed is computed from the committed diff (fail-closed), AC text must read as an outcome (hard validation), the operator is asked only when an existing AC changes or goes away, no single area owns a new AC (a lettered pick list in everyday words) or a new area is proposed, the catalog is read at the merge-base of --base-ref, answers go through a signed operator channel, the freeze is an append-only record compared with the catalog at finalize, and an unattended ask holds only its own unit when its question hashes recompute.
consequences: Exemption is a claim before the build; it is tested at F11 against the committed diff, as a warning that never holds a PR. answered_via and unattended are self-reported; the signature on an operator answer is a guard against accident and casual forgery, not authentication, and a determined agent with shell access can read the key. Built, pending operator decision: the brief's measure bar is not met and not measurable in this design (see the Q1 MEASURE file). The earlier lexical-HOW design replay is superseded. The superseded line in this run's own ac-record.jsonl is expected: it is the re-freeze of the stub.
rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-01: everything that code can decide is decided by code; AI only where code cannot decide.
rejected: A lexical HOW test as an ask trigger (false flags); hash-as-freeze (compare with the catalog instead); a wave-wide STRICT-STOP for a question; any label-based exemption; trusting a via field or an agent-typed autonomy flag
